newsitem.title: JAPAN: TEPCO reactor to start commercial operation July 2.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO reactor to start commercial operation July 2.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) said on Thursday its 1.36 million kilowatt (kw) reactor at the Kashiwazaki Kariwa nuclear power plant in Niigata prefecture will start commercial operations on July 2.
"The Kashiwazaki Kariwa complex will be the world's largest nuclear power plant once the unit starts," a TEPCO spokesman said.

The seventh reactor at the plant, on the Sea of Japan coast in northern Japan, will raise the total power generation capacity of the plant to 8.2 million kw, surpassing the Bruce plant in Ontario, Canada, which has a capacity of 7.3 million.

Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc, another regional power utility, is also planning to start commercial operations of a 1.18 million kw reactor at its Genkai nuclear power plant on Japan's southern island of Kyushu in late July.
